subject: Acme discovery — model fit & prompt-set collection
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme discovery — model fit & prompt-set collection

Jordan — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: help Acme migrate rule-based response flows to an LLM-backed assistant while keeping latency <= 300ms p50 for short queries and retaining strict PII redaction controls.
- Key constraints you mentioned: on-prem deployment for a subset of traffic, strict data retention window (30 days), and a heavy tail of short, high-frequency prompts from customers.

Suggested model fit (initial):
- For short transactional responses (FAQ, routing): a small quantized model variant (e.g., gpt-small-q8) to meet latency/cost targets.
- For context-heavy summaries and policy reasoning: a mid-sized model (gpt-medium/13B) with KV caching enabled.

Immediate asks for the prompt-set collection we discussed:
1) Please share ~200 representative prompts (CSV or similar) spanning: common short queries, multi-turn support threads, edge cases you see once a week/month, and any high-risk prompts containing PII patterns.
2) Mark redaction expectations per prompt (e.g., redact email, redact order IDs, keep last 4 digits). If unclear, flag as "needs guidance."
3) If possible, include expected-good / expected-bad outputs for 25-30 examples so we can use them as seed evals.

I attached a very small prompt sample template to show format expectations. Rishi and Monica — looping you in to help with the benchmark links and model recommendations; Rishi can pull the latency baselines from our recent retail use-case.

Next steps / timeline:
- Jordan: send initial prompt sample + redaction rules (aiming EOD tomorrow).
- Redwood: provide model recommendations + preliminary cost/latency estimates within 2 business days of receiving the prompts.

Thanks — feel free to hit reply all with any Qs.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: prompt_collection_template.csv (CSV template with columns: prompt_id,prompt_text,context,expected_output,redaction_notes)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ai-team@acme.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme discovery — model fit & prompt-set collection

Marissa — great summary, thanks. Quick notes and I'm attaching an initial dump of 120 prompts (redacted where we could). There are a few things to call out: 

- File attached: acme_prompt_samples.csv (contains prompts across our support, billing, and routing flows). We redacted full emails but left placeholders like [EMAIL_REDACTED]. Let me know if that meets your redaction needs.
- Edge cases: a set of prompts where customers include legal text or multi-paragraph policy quotes — those are tricky for summarization.
- Expected outputs: we included a few examples with preferred tone and mention of when to escalate to human ops.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) For redaction, do you recommend redacting order IDs entirely or token-masking (e.g., keep last 4 digits)? Concern is downstream traceability for support.
2) For benchmarking, what's the best way to submit multi-turn threads (we currently have many Slack-to-email chains)? CSV row per turn or consolidate as single conversation object?

Thanks — attaching the CSV now. If you want, we can also share a secure link to a small S3 bucket with raw logs (anonymized).

Jordan
Product Lead, Acme AI
jordan.lee@acme.com

Attachment: acme_prompt_samples.csv (120 rows, mixed single-turn and multi-turn examples with placeholders like [EMAIL_REDACTED])

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme discovery — model fit & prompt-set collection

Jordan — got the CSV, thanks for sending that over. Quick guidance and next steps from our side: 

1) Redaction recommendations (short):
- Order IDs / account numbers: retain last 4 digits only (token-mask everything else) — keeps traceability while minimizing exposure.
- Emails & full names: redact fully (replace with [EMAIL_REDACTED] / [NAME_REDACTED]).
- Payment info: redact fully.

2) Prompt formatting for best eval signal:
- For single-turn prompts: one row per prompt. Include a short context column when necessary (e.g., "user is on mobile app, purchased within last 24h").
- For multi-turn threads: include a conversation_id column and a single CSV cell that contains the concatenated turns separated by 
---TURN---
. That preserves ordering for our eval harness.

3) Seed evals: please flag 25-30 examples where you have a clear expected-good / expected-bad output. Those will be used as initial ground truth to detect regressions.

4) Model recommendations & benchmark links (prelim):
- Start with gpt-small-q8 for short transactional replies to hit latency/cost targets.
- Use gpt-medium-13B (with KV caching) for policy & summarization tasks.
- Benchmark doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBenchmarkDocs (contains latency/cost baselines and profiling notes).
- Public eval harness: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1423 (contains the template for our evaluation suite).

5) Quality/regression concerns: 
- We recommend running a small A/B eval between your current rule-based outputs and model outputs on key metrics: factuality, redaction fidelity, escalate-rate, and user tone. We'll generate a lightweight dashboard to surface regressions within 48 hours of receiving seed evals.

Attached: a filled prompt_collection_template.csv (small example) to show the conversation_id and turn delimiter.

If you can confirm the redaction masking approach (last-4 for IDs, full redact for emails/names), we'll proceed to run an initial bench on a 10% sample and share cost/latency estimates.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: prompt_collection_template.csv (filled example)
